title: selective-slo-mute-and-adaptive-shed-conservator
author: Jia Chen
release_notes: Introduces a selective SLO-muting mechanism and an adaptive shedding conservator to enable graceful, tenant-scoped degradation during transient overloads. Includes safety toggles and observability for rollout.
description:
Context: We observed repeated customer-facing latency spikes during multi-tenant surges where aggressive global SLO enforcement caused mass cascades (cascading rejections and region thrashing). This PR implements a conservative, tenant-scoped 'SLO mute' path together with an Adaptive Shed Conservator that performs gradual, measurable load reduction at the tenant level and coordinates with regional circuit states.
Motivation: Reduce noisy-neighbor sensitivity and avoid global circuit oscillation by providing a middle-ground policy between full circuit tripping and blind per-request rejections.
Design summary: 1) Selective SLO Mute: per-tenant soft-mute flag that temporarily relaxes SLO enforcement priorities for a defined window (configurable: duration, maximum concurrent muted tenants, max-mute-per-region). Muted tenants are served on a degraded but stable fast path with capacity reservations to avoid starvation of other tenants.
2) Adaptive Shed Conservator: a controller that monitors token-level latency percentiles, queue depth, and KV cache pressure and issues progressive shedding steps (10% -> 25% -> 50%) with hold and observe windows. The conservator prefers gentle request throttles, prefix-based caching, and prefetched slot reservation before rejecting.
3) Regional failover safety: when a region shows persistent degradation the conservator coordinates a soft handoff to neighboring regions with a staged warmup to preserve KV cache affinity where possible.
4) Safety & ops: global kill-switch, experiment flags, canary rollout config, and additional metrics/traces (slo.mute.{start,stop}, conservator.step, conservator.rollback_reason).
Checklist: - [x] Core conservator controller and state machine implemented - [x] Tenant metadata and API to request SLO mute (internal only) - [x] API guardrails (max concurrent mutes, TTL enforcement) - [x] Observability: metrics, traces, and dashboards added - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Release toggles and defaulted to off in config - [x] Docs: internal runbook and rollout notes
Commits: - feat(conservator): initial state machine, shedding steps, metrics (3 commits) - feat(slo-mute): tenant metadata, mute API and TTL enforcement - fix(region): preserve kv-drain tokens during soft handoff - test: integration tests for progressive shedding and regional warmup - ci: flake handling and new e2e scenario for noisy-tenants
Files changed (high level): - services/conservator/controller.go: New conservator controller, stepper logic and metrics hooks. Small excerpt: "if pressure.Score() > cfg.StepThreshold(step) { conservator.stepUp(step) }" - services/slo/tenant_muting.go: Tenant mute API, TTL enforcement, and in-memory lease store. - api/internal/admin_muting.md: Documentation for internal SRE use and runbook. - deploy/overrides/canary.yaml: Canary flags and parameters for rollout (defaults off). - telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml: Added slo.mute.* and conservator.* metrics and grafana panels. - tests/integration/noisy_tenant_shed_test.go: Integration scenarios with synthetic noisy tenants. - dockerfiles and minor CI config tweaks for longer e2e timeout.
Review conversation: "Miguel Ortiz (reviewer): Nice isolation of the stepper logic; please add a guard to prevent stepUp being called twice in the same evaluation window. Jia Chen (author): Added atomic lastStepSeen check and test; pushed 39c1a2. Ravi Patel (reviewer): Concerned about edge cases during regional handoff where KV affinity breaks. Can we preserve a small sticky slot reservation? Jia Chen: Implemented preserveSlots_on_handoff boolean and added tests to ensure at most 2 slots are sticky per muted tenant; pushed 7b9d4e. Elena Smirnova (reviewer): CI flake on noisy_tenant_shed_test; reran and added retry logic to the test harness. Post-review: Miguel approved, Ravi requested one doc clarification, which was added. CI: One integration test flake caused a rerun but final status is passing. Observability: Added dashboards and alert thresholds: conservator.stepRate > 5/min triggers a page until muted tenant decay completes. Runtime safety: The mute path is opt-in via canary and defaults to off. The conservator will not perform shedding if cluster-wide emergency_kill is active. Backwards compatibility: The feature adds new config flags and metrics but preserves existing runtime semantics when disabled. Migration: No DB schema changes; tenant mute metadata stored in a lightweight key-value placed in existing tenant-metadata store with TTL semantics.
Rollout plan: - Canary in staging for two days - Canary in us-west-2 with 1% traffic and SRE on-call for 48h - Ramp to 10% then 50% based on conservator.step/rollback metrics - Full enablement only after 7 days of stability
Observed performance in local integration runs: median p95 tail latency reduced by 12% for non-noisy tenants while noisy tenant throughput degraded gracefully (measured soft-shed steps).
Post-merge actions: - Ops to create canary override and runbook entry (docs updated) - Monitor conserve.step and slo.mute metrics during ramp - Prepare fast rollback if conservator triggers more than 3 rollbacks in 10m
Merge outcome: squashed and merged into main.
Changelog: Added to internal changelog under "Graceful degradation & conservator".
Notes: This PR intentionally keeps public API closed (internal admin only) for the first rollout. The code path is feature-flag guarded. If you are validating in staging and want to exercise the handoff path, use the canary override and the synthetic noisy-tenant scenario in tests/integration.
For follow-ups: - Expose tenant mute telemetry in Console for SRE playbooks - Add ML-driven step threshold tuning (future work ENG-4120) - Consider exposing limited self-service mute for enterprise customers behind explicit contract (product discussion required).
